title: Please support SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for build reproducibility
description:
Hello,

to generate reproducible builds, various distributions and toolchains support the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable.

https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/source-date-epoch/

Can you modify [`aaa.R` ](https://github.com/thomasp85/tweenr/blob/5f4ceb8a0d090142ec8da76b4c14e49d3573737e/R/aaa.R)to support it? The suggested way for `Sys.Date` in the URL above is:

```
if (Sys.getenv("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH") == "") {
  current_date <- Sys.Date()
} else {
  current_date <- as.Date(as.numeric(Sys.getenv("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH")) / 86400, "1970-01-01")
}
```

And for `Sys.time()` the equivalent is maybe:

```
as.POSIXct(as.numeric(Sys.getenv("SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH")) / 86400, "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")
```

This will allow us to distribute your package smoothly in Debian, were reproducible builds have an increasing importance. 

Have a nice day,

Charles

title: References or documentation for interpolation math?
description: Hello, Thanks for creating and maintaining this package! I'm trying to better understand the underlying mathematics implemented in the interpolators included in this package. For context, I work in an industry that requires verifying outputs from open-source functions prior to use, so I'm working on validating the numerical outputs of the main functionality of {tweenr}. **That said, are there any resources or documentation you can provide for the ways in which outputs are derived via the `tween_*()` functions?** In the reference manual, I see that for the `tween_numeric()` and `tween_numeric_t()` functions, the outputs should be equivalent to `stats::approx()`, for example, but based on the provided information I don't understand the conditions under which `stats::approx()` outputs match those of the {tweenr} functions. For example: ``` library(tweenr) tween_numeric(1:3, 3, ease = "linear") tween_t(data = 1:3, n = 5, ease = "linear") stats::approx(x = 1:3, n = 5) ``` returns the same outputs: But if I change the first argument in each of those function calls to `1:5` instead of `1:3`: ``` tween_numeric(1:5, 3, ease = "linear") tween_t(data = 1:5, n = 5, ease = "linear") stats::approx(x = 1:5, n = 5) ``` The outputs don't match: I'm also not sure how `grDevices::colorRamp()` can be used to verify outputs, though it's mentioned on the second page of the reference manual as a relevant built-in interpolation function. Any additional details, suggestions for comparisons, or references would be very helpful. Thanks in advance for your time! Arianna C. ``` > sessionInfo() R version 4.5.2 (2025-10-31) Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu Running under: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS Matrix products: default BLAS: /opt/R/openval/2026.03.00/4.5.2/lib/R/lib/libRblas.so LAPACK: /opt/R/openval/2026.03.00/4.5.2/lib/R/lib/libRlapack.so; LAPACK version 3.12.1 locale: [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8 [4] LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8 [7] LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NAME=C LC_ADDRESS=C [10] LC_TELEPHONE=C LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C time zone: Etc/UTC tzcode source: system (glibc) attached base packages: [1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base other attached packages: [1] tweenr_2.0.3 loaded via a namespace (and not attached): [1] compiler_4.5.2 magrittr_2.0.4 cli_3.6.5 tools_4.5.2 rstudioapi_0.17.1 [6] farver_2.1.2 vctrs_0.6.5 rlang_1.1.6 ```

title: values shifted over time
description:
This is my first bug report and hope I'm doing this correctly. Feedback is welcomed, and most off thank you for your free software and contributions


```r
# Reprex for tweenr
tribble(
  ~DATE, ~temp, ~humidity, ~wind_speed,
'2019-08-05 00:53:00',	75,	60,	6,
'2019-08-05 01:53:00',	73,	66,	5,
'2019-08-05 02:53:00',	71,	68,	8,
'2019-08-05 03:53:00',	71,	63,	10,

'2019-08-05 07:53:00',	73,	51,	5,
'2019-08-05 08:53:00',	77,	43,	5,
'2019-08-05 09:53:00',	77,	48,	7) %>% 
  mutate(DATE = ymd_hms(DATE)) -> in_dat

# create tibble with 15 minute increments
(add_mins <- tibble(DATE = seq(in_dat$DATE[1], in_dat$DATE[10], by = 900)))

add_mins %>% left_join(in_dat) # looks good

(add_mins %>% left_join(in_dat) %>% 
  tweenr::tween_fill(., ease = 'linear') -> test) # time now starts earlier

min(in_dat$DATE)
test %>% slice(17) # nearly the same time as first row (off by on sec, fine)
                   # but values for first row of in_dat are attributed to 
min(test$DATE)
```

title: `tween_t()` does not consistently place key positions when interpolating multiple variables
tween_appear not respecting timerange values
description:
Right now, setting the lower value of `timerange` doesn't affect the starting point of the tween. E.g.: 

```r
library(dplyr)
library(tweenr)

df <- data.frame(time = 0:10, val = 0:10)
tw_df <- tween_appear(df, "time", timerange = c(-1, 11), nframes = 100)

filter(tw_df, time == 0, .frame == 0)
```
returns 
```r
  time val .age .frame
1    0   0    0      0
```
when it should actually be returning 
```r
  time val .age .frame
1    0   0   -1      0
```
and 
```r
tw_df <- tween_appear(df, "time", timerange = c(1, 11), nframes = 100)

filter(tw_df, time == 0, .frame == 0)
```
returns 
```r
  time val .age .frame
1    0   0    0      0
```
when it should actually be returning 
```r
  time val .age .frame
1    0   0    1      0
```
I believe this can be solved in the `tween_appear` function by changing:
```r
timepoint <- f * framelength
```
to
```r
timepoint <- f * framelength + min(timerange)
```
In addition, I think that:
```r
framelength <- diff(timerange)/nframes
```
should be changed to:
```r
framelength <- diff(timerange)/(frames-1)
```
to ensure that the last frame ends exactly on the upper value of `timerange`. 

Of course, I might also have completely missed the point of what the code is intended to do, in which case you can safely ignore all of the above :-)

title: Inconsistent number of frames created by 'tween_state'
description:
I'm noticing that ``tween_state`` calculates one fewer frame if its ``.data`` argument is not the result of a prior "tween" than if its ``.data`` argument is the result of a prior "tween".  

For an example with three (identical) states stored in a list that is "reduced" by ``tween_state`` with ``nframes=2`` I'm observing no transition frame for the tween of the first two states and one transition frame for the tween of the second and third states.

```
> library("tweenr")
> df <- data.frame(piece_type = "pawn", color = "black",
+                  x = 1.0, y = 1.0, id = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
> dfs <- list(df, df, df)
> print(dfs)
[[1]]
  piece_type color x y id
1       pawn black 1 1  1

[[2]]
  piece_type color x y id
1       pawn black 1 1  1

[[3]]
  piece_type color x y id
1       pawn black 1 1  1

> fn <- function(df1, df2) tween_state(df1, df2, ease = 'linear', nframes = 2, id = id)
> df <- Reduce(fn, dfs)
> print(df)
   piece_type     color x y id .id     .phase .frame
1        pawn     black 1 1  1   1        raw      1
2        pawn     black 1 1  1   1        raw      2
21       pawn #000000FF 1 1  1   1 transition      3
11       pawn     black 1 1  1   1        raw      4
```

title: Making an animation using tween_appear()
description:
Hi

I am trying to create an animation of my first bicycle ride of 2017. I have a data frame with latitude longitude gradient and n (indicating the order of points).

I used `tween_appear()` to interpolate between the points but it is not clear to me how to use `.age` and `.frame` to create an animation with `gganimate()`.

Here is some sample code, I have dputted the data into a [gist](https://gist.github.com/padpadpadpad/7e58a5e0931897bbf8c0e0a4565ba96a) to save space in this issue.

The map in the code creates the animation for `lat_lon` as I could not work out how to do it with the `tween_data`.

```r
# data
lat_lon <- data_from_link

# make up new data using tweenr
tween_data <- tween_appear(lat_lon, 'n', nframes = 200)

# make a bbox
bbox <- ggmap::make_bbox(lat_lon$lon, lat_lon$lat, f = 0.3)
# get map
map <- suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(get_map(bbox, maptype = 'satellite')))

# plot of just the lat_lon data
le_plot <- ggmap(map) +
  coord_fixed(ratio = 1) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank()) +
  geom_path(aes(x = lon, y = lat,  col = grad, frame = n, cumulative = T), data = lat_lon, size = 2) +
  coord_cartesian() +
  scale_color_distiller('Gradient (%)', palette = 'Spectral') +
  facet_wrap(~ .frame)

animation::ani.options(interval = 1/24)
gg_animate(le_plot,  'first_ride_2017.gif', title_frame = F)

```

Any tips or help much appreciated.

title: NSE evaluation, similar to dplyr
description:
This package is excellent and I'll be interested in integrating it into the gganimate package!

Would you be open to changing `tween_elements` etc to take bare names instead of strings for the columns? For example, instead of

```
data %>%
    tween_elements('time', 'group', 'ease', nframes = 100)
```

It could be used like:

```
data %>%
    tween_elements(time, group, ease, nframes = 100)
```

This could be implemented as [described here](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lazyeval/vignettes/lazyeval.html), by making two versions of the functions, e.g. `tween_elements_` and `tween_elements`. The advantages:
- When used in a dplyr pipeline, people may be accustomed to using dplyr's, tidyr's, and ggplot2's use of bare expressions over passing strings of columns
- This API would be consistent with future features where people could perform operations in the `tween_elements` call, e.g. `tween_elements(time = round(year, -2)...)`, or where a bare string for `ease` would be interpreted as an argument (e.g. someone could just put `tween_elements(...ease = "cubic-in-out"... without having to add the`ease column to the data).
- People could still call `tween_elements_` if they wanted to provide string column names

**If you are open to this change, I would be very happy to implement it myself and submit it as a pull request**

title: Examples in README do not work anymore with last gganimate dev version
description:
Hi, 

In last dev version of [gganimate](https://github.com/dgrtwo/gganimate), @dgrtwo changed `gg_animate` to `gganimate` with more changes on the way GIF are saved.

It is a breaking change for `README.md` examples when we install with 
`devtools::install_github("dgrtwo/gganimate")`. We need to install last working version `dgrtwo/gganimate@26ec501` with `gg_animate`

As it is curently Work In Progress for `gganimate`, we maybe should wait for final work but as I wanted to try `tweenr` I stumbled upon these non working examples. 

I thought it would be valuable to report this.

title: Off-by-one error in `tween_elements()` when colors are included
description:
This can be illustrated with a slightly modified version of the dropping balls example:

```
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(20), y = rnorm(20), time = sample(100, 20), alpha = 0,
                colour = "goldenrod",
                size = 1, ease = 'linear', id = 1:20,
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d2 <- d
d2$time <- d$time + 10
d2$alpha <- 1
d2$size <- 3
d2$ease <- 'linear'
d3 <- d2
d3$time <- max(d2$time)
df <- bind_rows(d, d2, d3)

dt <- tween_elements(df, 'time', 'id', 'ease', nframes = 500)
```

This returns the error:
`Error in (function (..., row.names = NULL, check.rows = FALSE, check.names = TRUE,  : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 5432, 5431`

The problem does not occur if the color column is omitted. I'm not sure where exactly the problem is in the code.
